## [0.45.0] - Unreleased

Read before updating: this version upgrades the workspace database in a way
earlier versions refuse, and changes which files a request may send from disk.
Vayu now sends a request-body file only when you picked it in Vayu on this
machine or it lies under a folder allowed in Settings > Files, and nothing else
can claim a file was chosen.

### Changed

- **The workspace database moves to schema version 6** (#2356). Once 0.45.0
  opens a workspace, earlier versions refuse it, so going back to 0.44 means
  restoring a backup. The upgrade writes a copy of the database beside it
  first.
- **A file is sent only once it is picked on this machine or sits under an
  allowed folder** (#2356). Files you chose before updating are carried over if
  they still exist. A file on a drive or network share that is not connected
  when 0.45.0 first opens the workspace is not carried over, even once the
  drive is back; the engine log names each one. A request naming any other
  file outside an allowed folder, or one of those, says *Not chosen on this
  machine* and is refused at Send until you pick the file again (Relink) or
  allow its folder.
- **Typing a path no longer counts as choosing the file.** A path typed into a
  binary body is sent only after you pick the file or allow its folder; the
  editor says so as you type.
- **Settings > Files adds folders through the folder picker only.** The field
  for typing a folder path is gone, and the import preview's Allow folder
  opens the picker at the folder it suggests.
- **An engine already running when the app starts is replaced.** The app no
  longer adopts one it did not start this session, including one started by
  hand in development; it is shut down and a new one started on the same port.
- **Allowing or removing a folder, and recording a picked file, need the app's
  grant secret.** The app passes its engine a fresh secret in
  `VAYU_GRANT_SECRET` at every start. Without it, `POST` and `DELETE` on
  `/file-roots` and `/file-grants` answer `403`, so an engine run by hand, by
  the CLI or in CI cannot change which files are sent; folders and files
  already allowed still apply.
- **`unresolved` in a request body is ignored.** The engine works out whether a
  file may be sent and reports it as `unresolved` when it returns a request; a
  value sent by a script, an MCP agent or an older client is dropped.

### Fixed

- **A redirect loop and an undecodable response are no longer reported as
  "Couldn't connect"** (#2462). A send that exceeds Maximum redirects now fails
  with `TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`, and a response whose `Content-Encoding` its bytes
  are not in, or that Vayu cannot decode, fails with `BAD_CONTENT_ENCODING`;
  each message says which limit or encoding was involved. A script that tested
  `err.code` in `pm.sendRequest`, or `pm.response.errorCode`, against
  `'CONNECTION_FAILED'` for these cases now sees the new spelling. A load run
  records them as `too_many_redirects` and `bad_content_encoding`.
- **The raw request after a 301, 302 or 303 no longer shows a body the final
  request never sent** (#2462). A POST answered by one of these is re-sent as a
  GET without its body, and the raw request now ends at the headers to match.
  307 and 308 keep the body, and so does the view.
